findings.text: A newcomer learns right away what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. The opening paragraph does that job well.
findings.source: header, first lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The next step is easy to find: there is a link to it in the header. The steps themselves are concrete: clone, prerequisites, `./setup.sh`, then `athena ask "add a changelog"`. A newcomer knows what to do.
findings.source: header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the Next steps section

findings.text: The page demonstrates a study, but the suggested first try produces a code change. Nothing says how a study like this one is made or what a traced commit looks like. The demo and the product feel disconnected.
findings.source: Next steps: "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask \"add a changelog\"" vs header: "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project"

findings.text: After three header paragraphs, almost the whole page is a detailed state-machine study of a different tool. It covers exit codes 75 and 1, pending-close records and secondmates. A newcomer to Athena has to wade through a lot that does not help them decide whether to use it. "Start here" refers to firstmate, not Athena, which may mislead.
findings.source: Headings "Start here", "States of a piece of work", "Transitions" (t1–t12), "Counters"

findings.text: Several terms the page uses are explicitly left undefined. The "in scope" entry also admits it "gives no test for it." This is honest, but it leaves the firstmate explanation with holes a newcomer cannot fill.
findings.source: Glossary: "captain call — The firstmate source does not define a captain call." and similar entries for "durable record", "endpoint", "heartbeat", "wake"

findings.text: The same definitions appear twice, almost word for word, and the same rules come back in the bullets, the steps and the cards. The repetition makes the page longer without making it clearer.
findings.source: Start here, "Words used first" vs Glossary: entries for yolo, in scope, green, red and home

findings.text: Some of the page is internal bookkeeping: an owner-only link, a note about the repository folder and a remark about the study's own earlier misses. None of it is for a newcomer, and it adds noise.
findings.source: header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision"; About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/"; Limits f3: "A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths"

findings.text: The claim-to-source links do make the "traceable" promise concrete. A sceptical newcomer can check any statement against firstmate's files.
findings.source: Each statement ends with cites like "[c1]", and the claims link to e.g. "AGENTS.md:206-206" at the pinned commit
